result.summary: Configure Guix to build non-GUI Bitcoin Core release binaries (`bitcoind` and CLI utilities) for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux as static position-independent executables (`-static-pie`) linked against glibc 2.44. Add glibc patches to prevent non-deterministic `/gnu/store` paths in compiled binaries and disable runtime `dlopen` calls in NSS modules. Adapt `symbol-check.py` and `security-check.py` to validate static ELF binaries that lack an interpreter and dynamic library imports.
result.problem: Official Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux and on distributions with older glibc versions than the build target. Dynamic linking also complicates portability across diverse environments and prevents enabling certain security features like pointer authentication on aarch64 (issue #19075).
evidence: PR description: 'Release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (except for bitcoin-qt) are now compiled with `-static-pie`, making them more portable. They can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems than ship with older glibcs, than were previously supported.'

PR description: 'A side-effect of this change is that name resolution through dynamic nss modules is not possible. Users using mdns (.local), LDAP, or SSSD to resolve names for local connections should verify that connections are still resolved correctly.'
Fixes linked issue #19075 ('build: Investigate aarch64 pointer authentication').
result.scope_notes: Touches Guix build scripts, cross-compilation manifests, binary validation scripts (`security-check.py`, `symbol-check.py`), and applies source patches directly to glibc.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased following toolchain refactoring merges; no longer extracts toolchains into separate modules as that was done in prerequisites.
result.card: Configures Guix to build Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding bitcoin-qt) as -static-pie executables against glibc 2.44. This allows official Linux release binaries to run on non-glibc distributions like Alpine as well as systems with older glibc versions, and resolves issue #19075 for aarch64 pointer authentication. A known consequence is that runtime name resolution via dynamic NSS modules (e.g., mDNS, LDAP, SSSD) will not function. Symbol and security verification scripts are updated to validate static ELF binaries.

risk.why: Alters compiler and linker flags for official release binaries; defects could render release binaries non-functional on Linux platforms or break determinism across Guix signers.
